title: Identify imported code and pytest test module namespaces
applies_when: Python tests or benchmarks involve editable installs, multiple source roots, native/optional extensions, package-context imports or cached modules; registered CPU fixtures must precede production imports; parametrized wrappers, bound methods or mocks may change runtime identity; validation-tool pins differ; supposedly isolated tests use fixed ports or persistent files.
lesson: Inspect __file__ or __spec__.origin, callable module and native build in the actual interpreter; use fresh processes for ambiguous caches/search paths. Identical bytes under different module names create distinct class/exception identities: check at the consumer boundary, not only the path. Catching a probe's own exception does not validate an installed consumer. Direct imports do not register plugins: nested pytest -p anyio needs genuine distribution entry-point metadata pointing to the selected module. If the registered CPU entry prepares optional imports, run that fixture before inspecting origin, without replacing tested behavior. Keep collection/import errors separate from assertion failures. Non-package pytest test module basenames must be unique under prepend/append import modes; individually passing files can fail joint collection. Check new tests alongside neighboring modules using the repository's import mode, rather than switching modes to hide a collision. Record resolved dependencies and compare identical baseline/candidate tests and failure details; focused dependencies do not cover every suite. Patch mocks at the consumer binding with normal/error controls. Fresh processes do not isolate fixed ports; serialize or use network namespaces. Fresh URI/TMPDIR does not isolate hard-coded files: JuiceFS memkv reads /tmp/juicefs.memkv.setting.json independently of addr. Use a private backend/filesystem namespace, never clear another workload's fixture. Assert realized backend selection inside the test body, with reversed-order/fresh-process controls when wrappers retain their first runner. Cover functions and bound methods: assigning a function attribute can work while bound-method assignment raises AttributeError. The AnyIO/Hypothesis counterexample is scoped, not evidence against all parametrization.
avoid_when: A Python path does not identify a compiled extension or captured graph. Namespace/built-in modules may lack a source file, and diagnostic imports execute initialization. A single-module package-context rejection is a screen limit, not NO_BUG or execution authority. After review, use full-source roots and fresh processes; inspect optional dependencies too. A same-commit pure-Python shim is usable only with matching provenance/API. Match namespaces exactly (name == 'flashinfer' or name.startswith('flashinfer.')); a loose prefix also captures flashinfer_cubin. Source selection does not prove ABI compatibility; CPU optional-kernel fixtures do not qualify accelerator kernels or a server. Shared failure names do not prove equal causes or full qualification: retain details and consider interactions. Check tool --version and repository pin/config before acting on lint; a newer Ruff warning is not automatically a regression, nor harmless because it is old. Do not ignore rules or claim full-repository checks from two-file lint. A private venv is not an untrusted-code sandbox.

evidence.note: The PR records matched full-source, fresh-process native FP8-preparation tests using the same-commit JIT-cache shim: baseline 3 failed/2 passed, candidate 5 passed. This is focused invalid-argument correctness evidence, not full-suite, fused-kernel, performance, merge or prospective Scout-improvement evidence. A single-module relative-import block did not establish absence of the bug.

This pinned source declares ruff==0.14.10 for quality checks. It supports checking the validation-tool version as part of execution identity, not an unpublished bug, local pass, full repository qualification or proof that all newer diagnostics are spurious.

Python documents patching where an object is looked up rather than necessarily where it is defined. This is a test-boundary mechanism, not evidence that a mocked component run validates a full package.

The reported Hypothesis wrapper retains its first runner across parametrized backends. Check execution identity, not pytest's backend suffix. Existing PR #1354 addresses this issue; this lesson is not an independent approval of that fix.

Maintainer review explains why the proposed runner rewrap fixes ordinary functions but breaks bound test methods, and requests a class-method regression. Do not equate one repaired dispatch form with complete wrapper qualification. The review is public mechanism evidence, not acceptance of the current PR or a measured improvement to Scout.
The Python reference documents the module cache, search path and module specifications. These mechanisms explain source ambiguity; it does not validate any local installation or build.

Non-package test names must be unique under prepend/append. Importlib changes helper imports; do not switch project modes to hide collisions. Documented mechanism, not full-suite or discovery-yield evidence.

The native suite requires chardet, CLI/decoder extras and test tools beyond HTTPX's minimum runtime or focused URL environment. Tooling pins do not pin every runtime dependency; record resolution rather than assuming identical environments.

The official test instructions warn that suite servers use fixed ports 8000 and 8001. Independent Python processes on one host do not reserve independent endpoints. This supports a scheduling caution, not a measured throughput or general sandbox claim.

newMockClient reads a fixed absolute settingPath and does not use addr for fixture isolation. This source establishes the persistence mechanism, not a clean memkv run, a production defect or a measured Scout improvement. A fresh process, URI or TMPDIR alone cannot isolate that file.

The registered CPU entry calls maybe_stub_sgl_kernel before importing Req and the logprob processor. Pre-importing production in a diagnostic harness bypasses that fixture. The optional-extension adapter does not establish accelerator correctness.

The PR records complete-source CPU execution using the existing registered fixture: 36 tests pass; unchanged production fails four boundary subcases. This is local component qualification, not official CI, server/model accuracy, performance or measured selector utility.

Missing installed pytest entry-point metadata caused22 unrelated plugin-test failures. A normal private package install plus per-arm entrypoint/source identity checks enables54 selected Windows tests. Not a full backend matrix or measured Scout benefit.
